issues.failure_explanation: The Woodbury identity is misapplied in both expansions: the inner brace matrix must itself be inverted, and the scalar prefactor is wrong. The correct identities are (\tilde{\lambda}I_r+MM^T)^{-1}=\frac{1}{\tilde{\lambda}}I_r-\frac{1}{\tilde{\lambda}}M(M^TM+\tilde{\lambda}I_n)^{-1}M^T and (M^TM+\tilde{\lambda}I_n)^{-1}=\frac{1}{\tilde{\lambda}}I_n-\frac{1}{\tilde{\lambda}}M^T(MM^T+\tilde{\lambda}I_r)^{-1}M, whereas eq:wi1 and eq:wi2 state \frac{1}{\tilde{\lambda}^3} times the UNINVERTED matrices. Hence the displayed expansions are false equations and the proof does not establish the lemma as written. The lemma's statement is nonetheless true: for \tilde{\lambda}>0 both \tilde{\lambda}I+MM^T and \tilde{\lambda}I+M^TM are invertible, and (M^TM+\tilde{\lambda}I_n)M^T=M^T(MM^T+\tilde{\lambda}I_r) yields the identity directly; its later use in eq:errbound2 of thm:err_bound applies the correct identity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the Woodbury expansions with the inner matrix inverted and the correct scalar prefactors, or replace the proof by the one-line argument (M^TM+\tilde{\lambda}I_n)M^T=M^T(MM^T+\tilde{\lambda}I_r) with invertibility for \tilde{\lambda}>0; the statement and all uses then stand unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the proof of thm:woodberry_identity is defective: the intermediate identities eq:wi1 and eq:wi2 (and the derived eq:wi3, eq:wi4) are false as displayed. The lemma statement is correct and every downstream application (eq:errbound2 in thm:err_bound) uses the true identity, so no other result is invalidated.
issues.title: Woodbury expansion in the proof of thm:woodberry_identity is algebraically false (dropped inverses, wrong prefactor)
issues.why_classification: The lemma is true and the algebraic slips are routine local corrections (restore the dropped inverse and fix the prefactor); no inference, claim, rate, or regime downstream changes, so the repair is short and local.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof estimates \|\tilde{\lambda}(A_\tau^TA_\tau+\tilde{\lambda}I)^{-1}v\| \le \frac{\tilde{\lambda}}{\lambda_{\min}^{+}(A_\tau^TA_\tau)+\tilde{\lambda}}\|v\|, but for the typically rank-deficient block A_\tau one has \lambda_{\min}(A_\tau^TA_\tau)=0, so \|(A_\tau^TA_\tau+\tilde{\lambda}I)^{-1}\|_2=1/\tilde{\lambda}, not 1/(\lambda_{\min}^{+}+\tilde{\lambda}). Equivalently, the update factor \tilde{\lambda}(A_\tau^TA_\tau+\tilde{\lambda}I)^{-1} acts as the identity on \mathcal{N}(A_\tau), so the error component in \mathcal{N}(A_\tau)\cap\mathcal{R}(A^T) is never contracted and the claimed factor <1 is impossible. Concrete counterexample: A=((1,0),(1,1)), b=(1,2)^T, x_\star=(1,1)^T, block A_\tau=(1,0) (so \lambda_{\min}^{+}(A_\tau^TA_\tau)=1), x_t=(2,2)\in\mathcal{R}(A^T): then x_{t+1}-x_\star=(\tilde{\lambda}/(1+\tilde{\lambda}),1) and \|x_{t+1}-x_\star\|=\sqrt{1+\tilde{\lambda}^2/(1+\tilde{\lambda})^2} > \frac{\tilde{\lambda}}{1+\tilde{\lambda}}\sqrt{2} = \frac{\tilde{\lambda}}{\lambda_{\min}^{+}+\tilde{\lambda}}\|x_t-x_\star\|. The same failure defeats the iterated expectation bound, whose induction step is exactly this invalid inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem for the block-residual seminorm (valid because A_\tau(x_t-x_\star)\in\mathcal{R}(A_\tau), where A_\tau A_\tau^T has smallest eigenvalue \lambda_{\min}^{+}(A_\tau^TA_\tau)>0), or add the hypothesis x_t-x_\star\in\mathcal{R}(A_\tau^T); recovering a full-error rate requires a new argument over the orthogonality- and residue-based sampling of blocks.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central convergence guarantee for ROR-BK — per-step and expected linear contraction of the full error \|x_t-x_\star\|_2 at rate \tilde{\lambda}/(\lambda_{\min}^{block}+\tilde{\lambda}) — is false as stated. What remains valid is only the block-residual seminorm contraction \|A_\tau(x_{t+1}-x_\star)\\|_2 \le \frac{\tilde{\lambda}}{\lambda_{\min}^{+}+\tilde{\lambda}}\|A_\tau(x_t-x_\star)\\|_2; any claim of fast convergence of the iterates themselves is unsupported by this theorem.
issues.title: thm:err_bound contraction factor is false: the null-space component of the error is not contracted
issues.why_classification: The root is a single invalid norm estimate, and a local correction preserves a same-rate contraction for a natural seminorm, so no new global proof architecture is needed. But the advertised full-error linear rate and its iterated expectation form are withdrawn — a genuine loss of the theorem's main guarantee; this is a limited weakening to a recognizably comparable result rather than a collapse of the method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, when $x_k$ is an approximate solution of \eqref{eq:linear_system} obtained through \cref{algo:fabgmres_dobk}, it is the minimum residual-norm solution, since $x_k \in \mathcal{R}(A^T) \perp \mathcal{N}(A)$.

issues.failure_explanation: FGMRES minimizes \|b-Ax\| only over the affine Krylov space x_0+span{z_1,...,z_k} (via y_k=\arg\min_y \|\beta e_1-\tilde{H}_k y\|_2); it returns the global minimum-residual solution only if x_\star-x_0 lies in that space. The proof's final inference is invalid: x_k\in\mathcal{R}(A^T) (equivalently x_k\perp\mathcal{N}(A)) makes x_k the minimum-norm vector among all vectors sharing its residual b-Ax_k; it does not make x_k a minimizer of \|b-Ax\|_2 over \mathbb{R}^n. Hence the claim that FABGMRES with ROR-BK inner iterations gives a solution minimizing \|b-Ax_k\|_2 is false as stated.

failure_location.quote: FABGMRES with an inner iteration of ROR-BK (\cref{algo:fabgmres_dobk}) gives a solution $x_k \in \mathcal{R}(A^T)$ minimizing $\norm{b-Ax_k}_2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the claim as giving a solution x_k\in\mathcal{R}(A^T), i.e., the minimum-norm solution among all vectors with the same residual b-Ax_k, or delete the minimization clause; no change to the algorithm or its analysis is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The minimization guarantee attributed to the ROR-BK-preconditioned FAB-GMRES is withdrawn; the valid part of the remark (x_k\in\mathcal{R}(A^T), via thm:x_in_range_A_transpose) and the algorithm itself are unaffected.
issues.title: Unlabelled FAB-GMRES remark falsely claims the iterate is the minimum-residual-norm solution
issues.why_classification: A one-line rephrasing removes the false minimization claim while preserving the substantive range-membership conclusion; no rate, regime, or algorithmic guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is unsupported and partly ill-defined as stated. (i) The entire proof is a bare citation to Theorem 4.1 of [ReRBK] — an analysis of the TA-ReBlocK method — with no verification that its hypotheses cover the raw mean iterates of ROR-BK under the regularized weights W(S)=I_S^T(A_SA_S^T+\tilde{\lambda}I)^{-1}I_S; a necessary nontrivial argument is missing. (ii) x^{(\mu)}=\arg\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\|Ax-b\|_{\bar{W}}^2 is set-valued whenever A is rank-deficient (the paper explicitly targets underdetermined systems m<n), so the bound is ill-defined unless the minimum-norm solution in \mathcal{R}(A^T) is selected. (iii) The mean iteration obeys \mathbb{E}[x_{t+1}]-x^{(\mu)}=(I-\bar{P})(\mathbb{E}[x_t]-x^{(\mu)}) with \bar{P}=A^T\bar{W}A, and I-\bar{P} is the identity on \mathcal{N}(\bar{P})=\{v:\bar{W}^{1/2}Av=0\}; the rate (1-\alpha)^T therefore requires x_0-x^{(\mu)}\in\mathcal{R}(\bar{P}) (e.g., \bar{W} positive definite and x^{(\mu)}\in\mathcal{R}(A^T)), hypotheses not assumed.

failure_location.quote: The proof follows from the Theorem 4.1 in \cite{ReRBK}. Appendix at \cite{ReRBK} outlines the analysis of the convergence of $x^{(\mu)}$ to $x_\star$ as $m \rightarrow \infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define x^{(\mu)} as the minimum-norm (in \mathcal{R}(A^T)) minimizer, assume \bar{W}\succ0 (every row sampled with positive probability), and replace the citation with the fixed-point computation \mathbb{E}[x_{t+1}]-x^{(\mu)}=(I-\bar{P})(\mathbb{E}[x_t]-x^{(\mu)}) plus \|I-\bar{P}\|\le1-\alpha on \mathcal{R}(A^T), using that the eigenvalues of P(S)=A_S^T(A_SA_S^T+\tilde{\lambda}I)^{-1}A_S lie in [0,1).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised mean-convergence of ROR-BK iterates to a weighted least-squares solution (used in the introduction to motivate ROR-BK as a stable solver for uniform-sampling RBK) is unproven as written and ill-defined for rank-deficient/underdetermined systems; no other labelled result depends on it.
issues.title: thm:dobk_for_least_square_problems is unsupported as stated and x^(mu) is ill-defined for rank-deficient A
issues.why_classification: The statement can be saved by adding standard missing hypotheses (minimum-norm x^{(\mu)}, positive-definite \bar{W}) and a short fixed-point argument, so no new global proof architecture is required; but as written the proof is only a citation and the claim is ill-defined in the advertised underdetermined regime, which is more than a routine local fix.
